newsitem.title: NIGER: Slow start to Niger parliamentary poll.
newsitem.headline: Slow start to Niger parliamentary poll.

text.p: Polling for a new national assembly began slowly in Niger on Saturday with the main opposition boycotting the election -- the third parliamentary poll in three years.
As in previous elections, initial turnout in the capital Niamey was low but polling stations opened on time, witnesses said.
Police and Republican Guard were on duty at polling stations but despite July's turbulent presidential election there was no significant security presence on the streets of the capital.
An opposition front accuses President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, who seized power in January, of rigging the July election to ensure victory.
Like many of its neighbours in Sub-Saharan Africa, mainly Moslem Niger launched democratic reforms in the 1990s after the collapse of Communist rule in the Soviet Union.

It held presidential and parliamentary elections in 1993 but government became paralysed by squabbling between president Mahamane Ousmane and his prime minister Amadou Hama who was from a rival group which gained a majority in the 83-seat parliament.
Early parliamentary elections in January 1995 failed to resolve the standoff and Mainassara seized power a year later, drawing widespread international criticism.
Mahamane and Hama form part of the boycotting opposition alliance.
